Hi Samantha —

Great to hear — thanks for the traffic sample. I put together a concise onboarding sketch that addresses the four asks and a recommended timeline. High-level summary below; I’ll attach the full map as PDFs and a short quant-profile survey for your infra team to fill out.

Short answers (details in attachment):
- Batch sizes: start with target batching window 25–50ms, target batch sizes ~32–64 for request P95; adjust after week-1 profiling. Estimated p50 latency increase vs single-token baseline: ~5–12%.
- KV cache: enable prefix KV caching with per-session TTL 30–45s initially; extend TTL if conversation reuse > 40%.
- Quant profiles: begin with fp16 for canary; evaluate 4-bit (q4_0/q4_K_M) for steady-state after quality A/B tests — expect 20–35% token-cost reduction with modest latency improvement depending on kernels.
- Routing: default policy = latency-first for interactive endpoints, cost-first fallback to quantized model variants for non-interactive batch routes.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kickoff call (30–45m) this Wed or Thu — engineering + procurement + CS.
2) Red team (Redwood) runs 48h profiling against a 1% traffic sample (we’ll need API key + traffic CSV).
3) Week 1: tune batching TTLs, KV cache, and run quant A/B.
4) Week 2–3: roll steady-state routing and ramp reserved capacity if committed.

I attached: redwood_onboard_map_v1.pdf, quant_profile_survey.csv.

Would Thu 11/4 at 10am PT work for a kickoff? If yes I’ll send invites and loop in Monica (CS) and Rishi (engineer) for the detailed mutual action plan.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Thanks Kim. Draft mutual action plan below (short, actionable):

MUTUAL ACTION PLAN (BrightApps <-> Redwood)
1) Kickoff call — Thu 11/4 10:00 PT (owner: Customer Success / Kimberly) — confirm agenda: profiling scope, success metrics, procurement timeline.
2) Data handoff — BrightApps to provide 48-hour sampled traffic CSV + test API key by Fri 11/5 (owner: BrightApps / Samantha).

4) Quant A/B — run quality vs perf on fp16 vs q4 variants (owner: Redwood Research/Eng). Deliverable: quality comparison table, cost delta.
5) Canary + monitor — roll to 5% with canary monitors (token-cost, p95 latency, correctness score) then ramp to steady state; rollback triggers pre-defined.
6) Procurement decision checkpoint — recommended reserved capacity commit by Week 3 if cost wins are realized (owner: BrightApps procurement / Jordan).

Initial tuning recommendations (for call):
- Batch window: 25ms start; try 50ms window if p95 latency tolerable.
- Target batch size: 32–64; allow dynamic batching.
- KV cache TTL: 30s initial, extend to 90s if reuse observed > 40%.
- Quant candidates: fp16 (baseline), q4_0 and q4_K_M for cost tests.
- Routing policy: interactive endpoints default to latency-first cluster; background/async endpoints use cost-first quantized variants with 2x lower RU threshold.

I attached a compact monitoring template for the canary (canary-monitoring-template.xlsx). Rishi — can you add the expected GPU-hour cost for the 48h run and the resource pool we should allocate?
